heroHeadline: Day 75: 'El Cabo' (CJNG Teuchitlán Forced-Recruiter) Arrested in Coahuila — State Dept Reviews 53 Mexican Consulates; 34 Days to FIFA World Cup
heroSubtitle: Day 75 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). TEUCHITLÁN NETWORK COLLAPSE — MAY 7, 2026: FGR arrested Fernando Daniel Farías de la Cruz 'El Cabo,' CJNG's forced-recruiter for the Rancho Izaguirre / 'La Galera' compound in Teuchitlán, Jalisco — the extermination camp where forensic teams found nearly 100 DNA samples and bone fragments predating 2015. Arrested in Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila by the AIC on charges of enforced disappearances, crimes against health, and organized crime/human trafficking. His capture completes the methodical FGR dismantlement of the Teuchitlán operational chain: El Jardinero (Fractura Total commander, arrested April 27) → El Güero Conta (financial operator, arrested April 27) → El Cabo (recruiter, arrested May 7). STATE DEPT CONSULATE REVIEW — BILATERAL ESCALATION: The U.S. State Department began a formal review of all 53 Mexican consulates in the U.S. — the most concrete diplomatic escalation since February 22 — amid the now quintuple bilateral pressure track: CIA-Chihuahua sovereignty deadlock + DOJ Rocha Moya indictment + Sheinbaum's 'irrefutable proof' extradition standard (May 6) + State Dept consulate review + ongoing CJNG interdiction framework. SUCCESSION BINARY — DAY 75: Juan Carlos Valencia González 'El 03' (financial wing, confirmed leader — El País, April 6) vs. Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán 'El Sapo' (military wing, top-2 Federal Security Cabinet target — named May 3); El Sapo at large. DECAPITATION CAMPAIGN — 75-DAY LEDGER: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Doble R (arrested Mar 11), El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27, formally charged May 4 at Altiplano), El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27), El Cabo (arrested May 7). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials detained. WORLD CUP COUNTDOWN: 34 days to FIFA World Cup 2026 opening match (June 11, Mexico City). Guadalajara hosts 4 group-stage matches; Mexico's 130,000-person nationwide security deployment continues.
